name: Three Sisters Traverse

legs.route: Southeast ridge, crossing the Terrible Traverse and the Bowling Alley
North ridge, from the col south of North Sister
legs.connect: Descend North Sister's south ridge to the col, then climb the short glaciated north ridge of Middle Sister; late-season conditions showed no crevasse trouble.
Drop Middle Sister's southeast ridge to the glacier-melt stream at its base, then head west and climb South Sister's northwest ridge, skirting a steep rock step by touching the upper Eugene Glacier.

duration: 1 very long day, or 2 days with a camp
how: Usually done north to south so the technical peak comes first, while you are fresh: North Sister is the only one with real route-finding and loose rock on the Terrible Traverse and in the Bowling Alley. Middle Sister adds a short glacier crossing that needs an axe, crampons and a helmet. South Sister is a long talus slog by comparison. The fast version is about 19 miles and 9,400 ft of gain trailhead to trailhead. The reverse direction is also done.
descent: Walk out South Sister's graded climbers' trail to the Cascade Lakes Highway side, which is a different trailhead from the one on the north side where you start.
logistics: Needs a car at each end (Pole Creek on the north side, Devils Lake on the south) or a ride. Water can be refilled from glacier melt below Middle Sister. Best in late summer when the snow has thinned; a ski version is done in spring.
notes: Climber.org report rates the whole outing class 4 with glacier travel. FKT page gives 18.7 mi and 9,400 ft trailhead to trailhead, either direction. A user comment there says a permit is needed to summit; left out of app text, check current rules. Climberkyle report is a spring ski version that turned back below North Sister's summit.

name: Matterhorn and Sacajawea

legs.connect: Follow the crest over several gendarmes and an unofficial high point, passing most on the west side; a few moves may need the hands.

duration: 1 long day, or part of a 2–3 day trip
how: Most parties start from the Wallowa Lake side, hike to Ice Lake, then climb Matterhorn on a cairned path. The ridge to Sacajawea is class 3, with a few exposed class 4 moves that can be avoided; the rock is jagged and loose in places and a helmet is wise. Expect the ridge to take longer than its length suggests. Going the other way, from a Hurricane Creek camp, is also done.
descent: From Sacajawea, return to Ice Lake by scree and a creek, then out by the lake trail. If you finish on Matterhorn instead, the way down to the lake is steeper than it looks.
logistics: Many camp at Ice Lake and do the ridge as a day trip. Snow often lingers into early summer; water is available along the approach and at the lake. A one-way option from Hurricane Creek to the lake trail needs a shuttle.
notes: Class 3 per several reports; peakery commenter says class 3/4 and others mention exposed class 4 moves; higher kept as 'few class 4 moves'. Direction varies between reports. SummitPost pages returned 403 and were not read.
